assumptions: Upstream identity, frame hierarchy and camera intent remain authoritative outside the renderer.
limitations: This provider transports presentation coordinates only; it cannot create canonical positions, scientific truth, simulation state, identity, history or camera authority.

fidelity.validity: Hierarchical presentation-space transport with camera-relative precision and explicit frame boundaries.
fidelity.resolution: Float64 active/adjacent-frame CPU coordinates with Float32 high/low GPU projection when needed.
fidelity.uncertainty: Precision is bounded by the supplied upstream frame transform and does not improve source-model accuracy.

assumptions: Entity identity and provenance are supplied by upstream authorities and are preserved byte-for-semantic-byte by packet construction.
limitations: RenderPacket and RenderScene are GPU-neutral presentation contracts; they cannot promote provenance, mutate simulation state, or establish cross-GPU pixel identity.

fidelity.validity: Deterministic semantic packet composition independent of GPU backend and packet input order.
fidelity.resolution: Bounded scene packets with explicit geometry, material, picking and disposable-resource claims.
fidelity.uncertainty: Backend rasterization may vary across compliant GPUs while semantic packet identity remains deterministic.

assumptions: Feature detection truth is supplied by the browser/runtime environment and does not alter universe semantics.
limitations: WebGPU is an enhancement only in supported secure contexts; direct-file execution always requires the complete WebGL2 path.

fidelity.validity: Selects an interchangeable presentation backend without changing semantic scene identity or renderer authority boundaries.
fidelity.uncertainty: Backend availability is environment-dependent and is never inferred as scientific or product-semantic state.

assumptions: A supported secure-context WebGPU device/context is supplied by runtime feature detection; semantic scenes and camera matrices remain external authority.
limitations: Stage-1 WebGPU supports meshes, point batches and curves using unlit presentation color; unsupported packet families fail closed and WebGL2 remains the mandatory direct-file baseline.

fidelity.validity: Encodes actual WebGPU draw commands over the deterministic Deep3D semantic scene contract while retaining bounded disposable GPU resources.
fidelity.resolution: Triangle, line and point primitives; per-draw external view-projection and presentation color uniforms.
fidelity.uncertainty: Raster pixels are device-dependent; only semantic fingerprints and bounded command/resource behavior are deterministic claims.

assumptions: Upstream Deep3D packets already contain camera-relative presentation geometry and an external authoritative camera projection.
limitations: This checkpoint implements bounded mesh, point-batch and curve packet families only; unsupported Deep3D families fail closed and are not claimed complete until later convergence stages.

fidelity.validity: GPU-neutral Deep3D semantic scenes compile deterministically into the existing V2X-13 strict WebGL2 frame consumer without transferring authority.
fidelity.resolution: Triangle meshes, point batches and continuous curves with bounded V2X-13 resource lifecycle.
fidelity.uncertainty: Raster output is GPU-dependent presentation evidence; semantic scene identity is the deterministic contract.

assumptions: The V1X-04 source scene has already preserved canonical P3 identity and labeled noncanonical orbit presentation geometry.
limitations: Body mesh radius, color and orbit geometry remain presentation-only; current orbital phase and metric orbit distance are explicitly not claimed.

fidelity.validity: Converts the existing true-3D V1X-04 system representation into GPU-neutral Deep3D packets while preserving upstream identity and unknown handling.
fidelity.resolution: One bounded octahedral presentation mesh per rendered star/planet plus one curve packet per available presentation orbit.
fidelity.uncertainty: Body mesh size/color and orbital display geometry are visual encodings, not physical measurements.
